paper.title: Randomized Differential Testing of RDF Stores
paper.venue: 2023 IEEE/ACM 45th International Conference on Software Engineering: Companion Proceedings (ICSE-Companion)

summary.text: RD2 applies randomized differential testing to RDF stores, which serve knowledge graph and semantic web applications and answer SPARQL queries, and for which the authors say no logic bug detection tool existed. It builds an equivalent RDF graph across several stores and checks that they return the same result for a given SPARQL query. Queries are generated automatically from the SPARQL syntax and the generated graph so that they are syntactically valid and likely to return non-empty results, and result formats are unified before comparison. Across three widely used RDF stores it found 5 logic bugs.
summary.relationship_to_sqlancer: Differential logic-bug detection for RDF stores; SQLancer is cited among the database testing work it follows.
supporting_excerpts: However, no available tools can detect logic bugs in RDF stores.
In this paper, we propose RD2, a Randomized Differential testing approach of RDF stores, to reveal discrepancies among RDF stores, which indicate potential logic bugs in RDF stores.
The core idea of RD2 is to build an equivalent RDF graph for multiple RDF stores, and verify whether they can return the same query result for a given SPARQL query.

sources.excerpt: RAGS [14], APOLLO [31] and TAQO [32] utilize differential testing for detecting bugs in RDBMSs. SQLsmith [33] is used to detect bugs causing exceptions or crashes in RDBMSs. TLP [15], NoREC [16], PQS [17] and DQE [18] develop various test oracles to detect logic bugs and optimization bugs, and have found many bugs in popular RDBMSs. DT2 [19] and Troc [20] detect transaction bugs in RDBMSs.
